chunks: From him, from his father, from one of our companions who said:

Pigeons were mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a man said to him, 'It has reached me that Umar saw a pigeon flying and a man running under it, so Umar said, 'A satan running under a satan.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'What was Ismail among you?' So it was said, 'A truthful one.' So he said, 'The remaining pigeons of the Sanctuary are from a pigeon of Ismail.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the pigeons of the Haram in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the popular notion that the pigeons of the Haram are 'shaitan' by linking them to Prophet Ismail (AS), known as 'al-Siddiq', thereby establishing a sacred lineage for the birds. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual purity of the Haram's natural inhabitants, contrasting with the broader Islamic tradition that often views them as neutral or symbolic of jinn. The hadith serves to elevate the status of the pigeons from mere creatures to blessed entities associated with a major prophet.
